660:
(a) Prior to the start of the tattoo procedure, the artist should inspect his hands for hangnails, small cuts, sores, and abrasions. If a cut, sore, or abrasion is detected, a bandage shall be applied for added protection before gloving. Fingernails shall be trimmed to insure that gloves are not punctured.
(b) All jewelry such as watches, rings, etc., worn by the artist should be removed prior to the start of the tattoo procedure.
(c) Before working on each client, the fingernails and hands of the tattoo artist shall be thoroughly washed and scrubbed with warm water and bacterial soap, using an individual hand brush that is clean and in good repair. The hands shall then be dried by either an air blower or by single-use towels prior to beginning work on each client or when interrupted in the process.
(d) Single-use disposable latex examination gloves shall be worn by the artist during the tattooing process. Gloves shall be changed and properly disposed of each time there is an interruption in the application of the tattoo, the gloves become torn or punctured, or whenever their ability to function is compromised.
(e) Each artist shall wear a clean outer garment, apron or smock, which shall be changed after each client.
(f) Tattoo artists who are experiencing symptoms of diarrhea, vomiting, fever, rash, or skin infections shall refrain from tattooing activities.
(g) Adequate numbers of sterilized needles and tubes must be on hand for each artist for the entire day and night operation.
(h) Only single-use disposable razors shall be used to shave the area to be tattooed.
661:
(a) An operational sterilizer (autoclave) shall be provided in each tattoo studio.
(b) Used nondisposable instruments shall be kept in a separate puncture-resistant container until brush-scrubbed in hot water and soap, and then sterilized by autoclaving.
(c) The following procedures should be followed during the sterilization process:
(1) Prior to being placed in the autoclave all equipment shall be bagged, dated and sealed.
(2) Each autoclave bag may hold no more than one liner and shader tube with needle and bar inserted into tube.
(3) To protect needle tips from damage, an appropriate sterile protective covering shall be placed on the needle tip.
(4) Instruments shall remain in the autoclave 55 minutes from a cold start.
(5) If the process begins with a hot start then instruments should be processed for 35 minutes.
(6) To achieve proper sterilization, temperature must reach 273 degrees Fahrenheit and 15-30 psi.
(7) Spore indicators shall be used with each load to ensure spore eradication.
662:
(a) Before placing the tattoo design on the client's skin, the artist shall treat the skin area with an antibacterial solution.
(b) If an acetate stencil is used by a tattoo artist for transferring the design to the skin, it shall be thoroughly cleaned and rinsed in a germicidal solution for at least 20 minutes and then dried with sterile gauze or dried in the air on a sanitized surface after each use.
(c) If a paper-stencil is used by a tattoo artist for transferring the design to the skin, it shall be single-use disposable.
(d) If the design is drawn directly onto the skin, it shall be applied with a single-use article only.
663:
(a) The completed tattoo shall be washed with a single-use towel saturated with an antibacterial solution.
(b) After the area has dried, a thick layer of antibacterial ointment from a collapsible or plastic tube shall be applied.
(c) A bandage shall then be applied to the tattoo using a sealed Telfa (non-sticking) pad.
(d) The client should then be given written instructions on caring for the tattoo during the healing process.
664:
Each tattoo studio must be kept clean and sanitary. The owner must develop and implement a cleaning schedule that includes appropriate methods of decontamination and tasks or procedures to be performed. This written schedule must be based on the location within the studio, the type of surfaces to be cleaned, type of possible contamination present, the tasks or procedures to be performed, and their location within the studio. The following procedures shall be adhered to:
(1) Clean and sanitize all equipment and work surfaces with an appropriate disinfectant after completion of tattoo procedures and at the end of work shift when surfaces have become contaminated since the last cleaning.
(2) Remove and replace protective coverings such as plastic wrap and aluminum foil after each tattoo procedure.
(3) Inspect and decontaminate, on a regular basis, reusable receptacles such as bins, pails, and cans that have a likelihood for becoming contaminated. When contamination is visible, clean and decontaminate receptacles immediately or as soon as feasible.
665:
(a) Needles, razors, or other sharp instruments used during tattoo procedures, shall be placed in puncture resistant, closed containers immediately after use.
(b) Needles shall not be purposely bent or broken, or otherwise manipulated by hand.
(c) Containers of sharp waste shall be sent to a facility where they are incinerated or otherwise rendered nonhazardous.
(d) Disposable waste shall be placed in easily cleanable, closed containers provided with tightfitting lids to prevent leakage or spillage.
(e) Waste containers shall be kept closed when not in use.
(f) Disposable waste shall be handled, stored, and disposed of to minimize direct exposure of personnel to waste materials.
(g) The waste containers shall be located as near as feasible to the area of use. These containers shall not be overfilled.
666:
(a) Artists performing the tattoo operation shall obtain current certification in emergency first-aid, sterilization, and sanitary procedures.
(b) The artist must obtain a physical examination by a licensed physician within 12 months prior to employment or initial application for permit and repeated annually. The examination must be sufficiently comprehensive to assure that the artist is free of communicable diseases. To assure the artist is free of communicable diseases the following lab tests must be done at his expense: Hepatitis B and C, syphilis, HIV, and PPD and must be repeated annually. Proof of said exam must be furnished to the health department.
(c) The owner must maintain a file on all employees who perform tattoo procedures, which will be available for inspection and includes the following:
(1) Report of physical examination, including laboratory test results.
(2) Evidence of emergency first-aid, sterilization, and sanitation certification.
667:
(a) For each client, proper records of tattoos administered shall be maintained by the studio.
(b) Records of each client shall be prepared prior to the procedure being performed and shall reflect the client's name and signature, address, proof of age, date tattooed, design, its location and name of the artist.
(c) A statement of informed consent by the individual receiving the tattoo must be maintained on file for a period of three years.
(d) A statement by the client attesting that he is not under the influence of alcohol and/or drugs shall be on file.
(e) A copy of procedures signed by the client advising them of proper subsequent care of the tattoo shall be maintained on file for a period of three years.
(f) A copy of instructions signed by the client informing them of the risks involved and possible complications that might result from the tattoo procedure must be maintained on file for a period of three years.
668:
(a) The owner of each tattoo studio shall submit to the county health department annually an application for a permit to operate a tattoo studio under these rules and regulations. No tattoo studio shall be operated and no tattooing performed without a valid permit which is current under these rules and regulations.
(b) The application for a permit shall be made on forms provided by the health department.
(c) Each application for a permit shall be accompanied by a floor sketch of the tattoo studio showing windows, doors, room measurements, chairs, tables and equipment placement for clients and staff.
(d) A listing of the names of all staff including the owner who will be working in the studio shall be included with the application for a permit. This listing shall include the full name, current address and home phone number of each staff person.
(e) The ownership of the studio shall be fully disclosed in its application for a permit.
(f) Proof of compliance with zoning and other local requirements regarding the proper location and establishment of tattoo studios shall be furnished by the applicant prior to the issuance of a permit.
(g) The applicant shall certify in its application the name of employees or artists who are designated as being responsible for complying with the rules and policies adopted by the owner for the operation of the studio.
(h) The applicant must consent for the county health department to obtain his criminal history record information.
(i) The applicant shall attach to his application a copy of a written statement of policies and procedures outlining the responsibilities of management to ensure compliance with these rules and regulations.
(j) To offset the costs of application processing and inspection, a nonrefundable fee in the amount provided in the county fee schedule shall accompany each application for an original or a renewed license.
669:
(a) The owner of each tattoo studio shall obtain a valid permit from the health department prior to beginning operation and annually thereafter. To be eligible for a permit the studio must be in compliance with these rules and regulations.
(b) The permit shall be displayed in a conspicuous place on the premises.
(c) The permit is not transferable from one studio to another or from one owner to the other. Transfer of ownership shall also mean the transfer of a majority of the stock of a corporation, if the owner is a corporation.
(d) A permit shall no longer be valid and shall be returned to the county when the studio ceases to operate, is moved to another location, the ownership changes, or the permit is suspended or revoked.
(e) A studio which fails to comply with these rules and regulations shall be subject to the sanctions available to the health department pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 31-5-1 et seq. including but not limited to denial or revocation of its permit by the county.
670:
(a) The studio and its records shall be available for review and examination by properly identified representatives of the county during business hours.
(b) A copy of the inspection report shall be displayed in a conspicuous place on the premises and also shall be available for public inspection at the health department.
671:
(a) Enforcement of these rules and regulations shall be in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 31-5-1 et seq.
(b) No tattoo studio shall be operated without a permit. Failure or refusal to file an application for a permit shall constitute a violation of O.C.G.A. § 31-40-1 et seq. Any person who fails or refuses to file an application shall be subject to the penalties provided by law including, but not limited to, an order to cease and desist operating a tattoo studio.
(c) The health department may refuse to grant a permit for the operation of any tattoo studio which does not fulfill the minimum requirements of these rules and regulations and may revoke a permit which has been issued and invoke other sanctions if a studio violates any of these rules and regulations. (d) The health department is empowered to institute appropriate proceedings in a court of competent jurisdiction for the purpose of enjoining violation of any applicable provision of O.C.G.A. § 31-1-1 et seq., or of these rules and regulations.

Applicant means the owner of land submitting an application for development.

j. Adjusting and repairing brakes;
k. Minor motor adjustments not involving removal of the head or crankcase or racing the motor;
l. Sales of cold drinks, packaged foods, tobacco and similar convenience goods for station customers as accessory and incidental to the principal operation; and
m. Provision of road maps and other informational material to customers;
n. Provision of restroom facilities.

b. Straightening of body parts;
c. Painting;
d. Welding;

Building area means the total areas taken on a horizontal plane at the main grade level of the principal building and all accessory buildings, exclusive of uncovered porches, terraces and steps.
Building area of a lot means that portion of a lot bounded by the required rear, side and front building setback lines.

Building inspector means the authorized building inspector for the county.
Building line means the line beyond which a building shall not extend as determined by front, side, and rear yards defined herein.
Building, main, means a building in which is conducted the principle use of the lot on which it is situated. In any residential district, any dwelling shall be deemed to be a main building on the lot on which it is situated.
Building permit means a written permit issued by the county zoning administrator or building inspector.
Building setback, front, means the minimum allowable distance between the centerline of an abutting street, or an official future street, and the front of a building or structure on a lot. Building setback, side, means the minimum allowable distance between the side property line and a building or structure on a lot. The side setback applies to and extends the full depth of the lot.
Building site means the ground area of a building or buildings together with all open spaces surrounded by said building or buildings.
Care home means a rest home, nursing home, convalescent home, home for the aged or similar use established and operated to provide lodging and meals or domiciliary care for aged, infirm, chronically ill or convalescent persons.

Child care center, family, means a private residence operated by any person who receives for pay therein for supervision and care fewer than 24 hours a day, without transfer of legal custody, at least three but not more than six children under 18 years of age who are not related to such persons and whose parents or guardians are not residents in the same private residence.
Child care center, group, means any place operated by any person or group wherein for pay are received not less than seven nor more than 18 children under 18 years of age for care and supervision less than 24 hours a day.
Clinic means an establishment where medical or dental patients, who are not lodged overnight, are admitted for examination or treatment.
Club, church orfraternal organization means buildings and facilities owned or operated by a corporation, association, person or persons for a social, educational, religious or recreational purpose, but not primarily for profit or to render a service which is customarily a business.
Commercial use means any use involving in part or in whole, the storage of merchandise, sale of merchandise, materials or services, but not including home occupations, as defined in this section.
Communications tower means a tower of any size which supports communication equipment (transmission or receiving) utilized by commercial, government, or other public and quasi-public users. Comprehensive plan means the comprehensive land use plan for the county adopted by the board of commissioners under O.C.G.A. § 36-70-3.
Conditional use means a use permitted in a particular zoning district only upon showing that such use in a specified location will comply with all conditions and standards for the location or operation of such use as specified in this chapter and authorized by the county planning and zoning board.
Convenience establishment means a convenience gas station or a convenience store as defined in this section.

Convenience store means a one-story, retail store that is designed and stocked to sell primarily food, beverages, household supplies and other convenience goods on a small-scale basis.
Customary home occupation means a business, profession, occupation, or trade conducted for gain or support by any occupant of a dwelling and located entirely within a residential building or a structure accessory thereto, which use is accessory, incidental, and secondary to the use of the building for dwelling purposes and does not change the essential residential character or appearance of such building.
Dedicated to public use means land or improvements that have been deeded to and accepted by the county for public use and maintenance.
Developer means a person who is responsible for any undertaking that requires a building permit, conditional use permit or sign permit.
Director and engineer include the term "designee."
Drive-in means a retail or service enterprise oriented to automobile driving patrons wherein service is provided to the consumer on the outside or inside of the principal building. Dwelling means any building or portion thereof, which is designed or used exclusively for permanent living quarters for one or more persons.

Easement means a strip of land on which a property owner has granted a person, corporation or governing authority the right to use such land for a specific purpose.

Evidence means any testimony, document or other items which may be admissible, pursuant to state law in any trial or hearing conducted in any court of this state.
Family means one or more persons occupying a single dwelling unit; provided that, unless all members are related by blood, legal adoption or marriage, the dwelling unit shall contain no more than five persons; and further provided that domestic servants employed on the premises may be housed on the premises.

Filling station means any building or premises used solely for the storing, dispensing, servicing, sale or offering for sale at retail of any automobile fuels and lubricants or automobile accessories but not including major automobile repairing.
Floodplain means any land area susceptible to be inundated by water from the base flood. Major road plan means any legally adopted plan for the future development or classification of major roads in the county.
Manufactured home means a structure defined by and constructed in accordance with the federal Manufactured Home Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974 as amended 42 USC 5401 et seq., adopted June 15, 1976. The definition is as follows:
Manufactured home means a structure, transportable in one or more sections, which, in the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length, or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet, and which is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air-conditioning and electrical systems contained therein; except that such term shall include any structure which meets all the requirements of this paragraph except the size requirements and with respect to which the manufacturer voluntarily files a certification required by the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development complying with the standards established under this title.
Map or zoning map means the official county zoning map.
Master sewerage plan means the long-range master plan for the development of public sewerage systems as adopted by the board of commissioners.
Mobile home, as provided in O.C.G.A. § 8-2-160, means a structure, transportable in one or more sections, which, in the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet and which is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities and includes the plumbing, heating, air-conditioning and electrical systems contained therein; except that such term shall include any structure that meets all the requirements of this definition except the size requirements and with respect to which the manufacturer voluntarily files a certification required by the secretary of housing and urban development and complies with the standards established under the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, 42 USC 5401 et seq.
Modular home. See Industrialized building.
Motel means any building containing sleeping rooms for more or less temporary occupancy of individuals who are lodged with or without meals and where the design favors a direct vehicular approach to each sleeping or living room. Any building or structure exceeding two stories in height shall be classified as a hotel rather than a motel.
Natural grade means the elevation of the ground adjoining the building.
Neighborhood shopping center means a shopping center which consists entirely or primarily of convenient goods outlets with a supermarket as anchoring tenant. Neighborhood shopping centers generally do not have enclosed air-conditioned malls, elaborate landscaping and similar amenities typical of larger shopping centers.
Nonconforming lot means a lot existing at the effective date of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived (and not created for the purposes of evading the restrictions of this chapter) that does not meet the minimum area requirements of the district in which the lot is located.
Nonconforming use means any building, structure or use of land existing at the time of enactment of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived which does not comply with or conform to the provisions of the zoning district in which it is located. Nonconforming signs shall be governed by the provisions of article XIII, regarding nonconforming uses, and chapter 30, regarding signs.
Off-site means any premises not located within the area of the property to be subdivided whether or not in the same ownership of the applicant for subdivision approval.
Off-street loading space means the area required to load or unload goods or other materials plus the necessary driveways and maneuvering areas.
Off-street parking space means the area required to park one automobile plus the necessary driveways and maneuvering areas.
On-site disposal means the disposal of sewage from an individual use into the ground, a septic tank, or elsewhere except into a public or private sewerage system.
Open space means a parcel or parcels of land or an area of water or a combination of both land and water within the designated development and designed and intended for the use and enjoyment of residents of the development or for the general public, not including streets or off-street parking areas. Open space shall be substantially free of structures, but may contain such improvements as are in the plans as finally approved and are appropriate for the benefit of residents of the development.
Parcel means a general term including all plots of land shown with separate identification on the official tax appraisal maps. Parcels may or may not be lots, depending upon whether or not such parcels are created as herein provided.
Parking lot means a parcel of land devoted to unenclosed parking spaces which may include partially enclosed one-story buildings and where a charge is made for storage or parking of vehicles.
Permitted use means a use by right which is specifically authorized in a particular zoning district.
Personal care means protective care and watchful oversight of a resident who needs a watchful environment but who does not have an illness, injury or disability which requires chronic or convalescent care including medical and nursing services. The term "protective care and watchful oversight" includes but is not limited to a daily awareness by the care provider of the resident's functioning, his whereabouts, the making and reminding a resident of appointments for medical checkups, the ability and readiness to intervene if a crisis arises for a resident, supervision in areas of nutrition and medication, and actual provision of transient medical care, with a 24-hour responsibility for the well-being of the resident.
Personal care home means a building occupied as a permanent primary residence and also occupied by up to five unrelated ambulatory adults who reside there temporarily or long-term and receive services, including room, meals and personal care from the permanent occupants. The term "personal care home" does not include buildings which are devoted to independent living units which include kitchen facilities in which residents have the option of preparing and serving some or all their own meals or boarding facilities which do not provide personal care.
Planned center, office, commercial, or industrial, means a group of three or more retail stores, service establishments, offices, industries or any other businesses planned to serve the public, which is in common ownership or condominium ownership.
Planned unit development means any planned concentration which provides for innovative concepts in large-scale residential, commercial, or industrial development which enables economy in capital expenditures or utilities and streets and in subsequent maintenance.
Planning and zoning board means the county planning and zoning board.
Plat, final, means the plat submitted to the planning and zoning board for final approval and, subsequently, to be recorded with the county clerk of the superior court.
Plat of record means an abbreviated version of the final plat of a subdivision that is prepared as required by these regulations for filing, and is so filed, with the clerk of the superior court.
Plat, preliminary, means the plat or layout of a proposed subdivision submitted to the planning and zoning board for approval prior to submission of the final plat.
Principal building means a building in which is conducted the principal use of the lot or tract of land on which such building is located.
Principal use means the primary use of land or structures as distinguished from a conditional use or accessory use.
Private sewerage means a sanitary sewerage system for the collection of waterborne wastes complete with a sewage treatment plant or stabilization pond which is owned and operated by a person or corporation other than a public authority or agency.
Public hearing means a meeting announced and advertised in advance and open to the public, with the public given an opportunity to talk and participate.
Public improvement means any drainage ditch, roadway, parkway, sidewalk, pedestrian way, tree, lawn, off-street parking area, lot improvement, or other facility for which the local government may ultimately assume the responsibility for maintenance and operation, or which may affect an improvement for which local government responsibility is established.
Public notice means a notice published once in a newspaper of general circulation in the country at least 15 days prior to a public hearing setting forth the time, place and purpose of said public hearing concerning:
(1) Proposed changes or amendments to this chapter including the maps thereto;
(2) Appeals, variances or conditional use permits; or
(3) Review of a preliminary plat.
Public sewerage means a sanitary sewerage system for the collection of waterborne wastes complete with a sewage treatment plant or stabilization pond which is owned and operated by a public authority or agency.
Public utilities means water, gas, sanitary and storm sewer, electrical, and communication lines and facilities, and natural or improved drainage facilities.
Registered land surveyor means a land surveyor properly licensed and registered in this state.
Right-of-way line means a strip of land occupied or intended to be occupied by a street, crosswalk, railroad, road, electric transmission line, oil or gas pipeline, water main, storm or sanitary sewer main, shade trees, or for another special use, and owned by a county or municipality.
Rural street or rural road means a street supplementary to the major street system which primarily serves agricultural areas or other lands not subdivided for residential use.
Screening means either:
(1) A strip of at least ten feet wide, densely planted (or having equivalent natural growth) with shrubs or trees at least four feet high at the time of planting, of a type that will form a yearround dense screen at least six feet high; or
(2) An opaque wall or barrier or uniformly painted fence at least six feet high.
Setback means the required distance between a structure and the lot lines on the lot in which the structure is located. Lot lines can be the property lines or the edge of a street right-of-way.
Shoulder means that portion of a roadway between the outer edge of the paved surface or the curb to the inside edge of the ditch or gutter or original ground surface.
Sidewalk means that portion of a street or road right-of-way available exclusively for pedestrian traffic.
Sketch plat or site plan means a generalized map prepared by the developer that shows the development concept. Its purpose is to serve as a basis for discussion without either the planning and zoning board or the developer making commitments.
Street means a right-of-way for vehicular traffic whether designated a street, highway, thoroughfare, parkway, road, avenue, drive, expressway, freeway, boulevard, lane, place, circle, alley, or otherwise. Various types of streets may be defined as follows:
Arterial street means a public way which is used primarily for fast and heavy traffic flow; is of considerable continuity; and is used as a traffic artery for intercommunication among large areas.
Collector street means a major street used for traffic of moderate speed and high peak volumes between land service streets and arteries or serving as principal entrance streets or primary circulation routes within a subdivision, neighborhood or other limited area.
Cul-de-sac means a local street with only one outlet, closed and terminated by a vehicular turnaround. It shall not extend to more than 700 feet in length and shall be provided with a turnaround having a roadway diameter of at least 80 feet and a right-of-way diameter of at least 100 feet.
Local street means a street used primarily in residential subdivisions for access to abutting properties as opposed to the collection and dispersion of traffic.
Marginal access street means a street which is parallel or adjacent to an arterial street or highway and which provides access to abutting properties and protection from through traffic.
Private street means private access from a public road to land abutting on the right-of-way thereof; a street that has not been accepted by the county.
Street, county, means a street which is owned or maintained by the county.
Street grade means the grade of the curb or centerline of a street measured at any point along the street.
Street width means the shortest distance between the lines delineating the right-of-way of a street.
Structural alterations means any change in the supporting members of a building or structure, such as bearing walls, columns, beams, girders, floor joists or roof joists, or in the exterior walls.
Structure means anything constructed or erected with a fixed location on or in the ground, or attached to something having a fixed location on the ground. Structures include, but are not limited to the following: site-built buildings, industrialized buildings, manufactured homes, billboards, swimming pools, advertising signs, satellite dishes and fall-out shelters.
Subdivider means any person, firm or corporation, or the authorized agent of such person, firm or corporation, having such a proprietary interest in the land to be subdivided so as to have authority to authorize the maintenance of proceedings to subdivide such land under these regulations.
Subdivision means the division of a lot, tract or parcel of land into two or more lots, plats, sites or other divisions of land for the purpose, whether immediate or future, of sale or of building development for purposes other than agricultural. It includes all such subdivision of land involving new streets or a change in existing streets and includes resubdivision.
Subdivision improvement agreement means a contract entered into by the applicant and the planning and zoning board on behalf of the county by which the applicant promises to complete the required public improvements within the subdivision within a specified time period following final subdivision plat approval.
Surveyor means a registered, practicing surveyor, licensed by the State of Georgia.
Tower means any structure whose principal function is to support an antenna.
Tract means a lot. The term "tract' is used interchangeably with the term lot, particularly in the context of subdivisions, where one tract is subdivided into several lots.
Travel trailer means a vehicular portable structure built on a chassis, designed to be used as a temporary dwelling for travel and recreational purposes, and having a body width not exceeding eight feet.
Travel trailer park means any plot or tract of land on which two or more travel trailers are located or intended to be located for purposes of temporary occupancy.
Tree means any object of natural growth.
Use means the purpose for which land or a building or other structure is designed, arranged or intended for which it is or may be occupied or maintained.
Used or occupied, as applied to any land or building, shall be construed to include the term "intended," "arranged," or "designed to be used or occupied."
Utility facilities means any above-ground structures or facilities other than buildings, unless such buildings are used as storage incidental to the operation of such structures or facilities, owned by a governmental entity, a nonprofit organization, a corporation, or any entity defined as a public utility for any purpose by the appropriate provision of state law and used in connection with the production, generation, transmission, delivery, collection, or storage of water, sewage, electricity, gas, oil, or electronic signals.
Variance means an alteration or relaxation of the terms of these regulations where such alteration will not be contrary to the public interest, convenience and welfare; where owing to conditions peculiar to the property over which the applicant for a variance has no control, a literal enforcement of these regulations would create unnecessary and undue hardship.
Yard means an unoccupied area of a lot, open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky, except as otherwise provided in this chapter.
Yard, front, means an open space extending the full width of a lot and of a depth measured horizontally at right angles from the front lot line to the front of the structure.
Yard, rear, means an open space extending the full width of a lot and of a depth measured horizontally at right angles from the rear lot line to the rear of the structure.
Yard, side, means an open space extending along the side line of a lot between the front yard and the rear yard and of a width measured horizontally at right angles from the side lot line to the side of the structure.
Zoning administrator means the county tax assessor or any other individual or agency designated by the board of commissioners to administer this chapter.
Zoning change means an action by the board of commissioners causing a change in the boundary of a zoning district so as to change the zoning designation on a property or a portion of a property, or cause the establishment of a conditional use on a property.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. II, §§ 2-1, 2-2; Policy of 1-6-2020; Policy of 7-9-2024(1))
687:
The board of commissioners has adopted the Jefferson County Joint Comprehensive Plan, 2009, a copy of which is available in the office of the city clerk.
(Res. of 5-3-2010)
691:
(a) O.C.G.A. title 36, ch. 67A (O.C.G.A. § 36-67A-1 et seq.) requires disclosure of financial interests by all government officials, including board of commissioners members and planning and zoning board members, who will consider a rezoning action. It also requires disclosure of campaign contributions or gifts by the rezoning applicant or his attorney.
(b) All government officials, including board of commissioners members and planning and zoning board members, are required to disclose in writing any ownership interest they have or any family members have in real property made the subject of a rezoning request. Additionally, these officials are required to disclose in writing any financial interest of ten percent or more in any business entity which has an ownership interest in the property to be considered.
(c) An applicant for a rezoning and his attorney must disclose all campaign contributions or gifts aggregating $250.00 or more that were made within two years of the filing of the application for rezoning.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. I, § 1-5)
692:
Whenever a violation of this chapter occurs, or is alleged to have occurred, any person may file a written complaint. Such complaint stating fully the causes and basis thereof shall be filed with the zoning administrator. He shall record properly such complaint, immediately investigate and take action thereon as provided by this chapter.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-8)
693:
Any party aggrieved because of the alleged error in any order, requirement, decision, or determination made by the planning and zoning board, the board of commissioners, or any other party in the enforcement of this chapter, may take an appeal to the county superior court. The appeal to the superior court shall be the same as an appeal to the superior court from any decision made by the court as specified in O.C.G.A. title 15, ch. 6, art. 2 (O.C.G.A. § 15-6-50 et seq.); provided, however, that said appeal must be filed within 30 days from the date of the decision of the planning and zoning board, the board of commissioners or of any official charged with the enforcement of any order, requirement or decision in connection therewith; and upon failure to file said appeal within 30 days, said decision of the board of commissioners or planning and zoning board shall be final.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-9)
694:
(a) Any person found in violation of any provision of this chapter shall be subject to a fine of not more than $500.00 per violation or imprisoned in the county jail for not more than 60 days, or both, and in addition shall pay the cost of such action. Each offense shall constitute a separate offense for each day such violation continues.
(b) The county, through its attorney or other official designated by the governing authority of the county, may, in addition to other remedies, institute an injunction, mandamus or other appropriate action or proceeding to enforce the provisions of this chapter.
(c) Any building erected in violation of this chapter shall be deemed an unlawful structure, and the building inspector, county attorney, or other official designated by governing authority of the county may bring appropriate action to enjoin such erection or cause it to be vacated or removed.
(d) To enforce the provisions of this chapter, when a violation has occurred, a citation and summons may be issued to the alleged violator, requiring him to appear in the county magistrate court or state court on a day and time certain to answer the charges contained herein.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-7)
695:
The board of commissioners shall hear and make decisions concerning:
(1) Proposed amendments to this chapter;
(2) Adoption and amendment to the zoning map and the text of this chapter; and
(3) Approval, disapproval or other action on all requests for zoning changes as provided in this chapter.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. III, § 3-2)
696:
(a) The provisions of this chapter shall be administered and enforced by the zoning administrator or other designated county official. This official shall have the right to enter upon any premises for the purpose of making inspections of buildings or premises necessary to carry out his duties in the enforcement of this chapter. In addition, he shall issue all building permits and make and maintain records thereof, issue all certificates of occupancy and make and maintain records thereof, and conduct inspections as prescribed by this chapter and other such inspections as are necessary to ensure compliance with this chapter.
(b) Specifically, but without limitation, the zoning administrator shall have the power and duty to provide the following services related to this chapter:
(1) Issue and when necessary revoke building permits as specified in this chapter.
(2) Issue a certificate of occupancy as required in this chapter.
(3) Issue and when necessary revoke a moving permit (building permit) as specified in this chapter.
(4) Issue a sign permit as specified in this chapter.
(5) Answer all questions of interpretation of the provisions of this chapter.
(6) Administer the provisions of this chapter.
(7) Meet with a developer, if requested, during a pre-application conference to discuss a development proposal as defined in this chapter.
(8) Dispense general information about this chapter to the public upon request.
(9) Enforce, in addition to the enforcement authority of other county officials such as the county marshal, the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. III, §§ 3-3, 13-5)
697:
The building inspector shall have duties and responsibilities as assigned by the zoning administrator.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. III, § 3-4)
700:
There shall be a planning and zoning board consisting of five members. The purpose of the planning and zoning board is to provide informal consultation and formal proceedings for owners wishing to appeal a decision of the zoning administrator, or receive a conditional use permit, receive a variance or subdivide land.
(Ord. No. 006-95, 4-11-1995; Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. III, § 3-1)
701:
(a) Planning and zoning board members shall be appointed by the board of commissioners. For the purpose of appointing members to the planning and zoning board, the county shall be divided into four districts which shall be coterminous with board of commissioners' districts. An effort shall be made to provide one member of the planning and zoning board from each district. The fifth member shall be appointed from the county at large. The planning and zoning board shall annually elect one of its members as chairperson.
(b) The members shall be appointed for overlapping terms of three years. The board of commissioners shall have the right to remove any member of the planning and zoning board for cause.
(Ord. No. 006-95, 4-11-1995; Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. III, § 3-1.1)
702:
Meetings of the planning and zoning board shall be at the call of the chairperson and at such other times as the board may determine.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. III, § 3-1.2)
703:
The planning and zoning board shall not have the power to amend these regulations, to rezone any land, to declare this chapter or any amendment thereto invalid or to allow any use not permitted by this chapter. The duties of the planning and zoning board shall include, without limitation:
(1) Recommending to the board of commissioners changes in this chapter that the planning and zoning board believes are appropriate.
(2) Recommending to the board of commissioners approval, disapproval or other action on all requests for zoning changes as provided in this chapter.
(3) Reviewing and approving all plats.
(4) Reviewing and approving all subdivision developmental plans.
(5) Advising the board of commissioners on matters of zoning and land development as it may deem appropriate.
(6) Hearing and deciding appeals as specified in this chapter, where it is alleged by the appellant that there is an error in any order, requirement, permit, decision, determination or refusal made by the zoning administrator or other administrative official in the carrying out or enforcement of any provisions of this chapter.
(7) Hearing and deciding applications for a conditional use permit as specified in this chapter.
(8) Hearing and deciding questions involving interpretation of the zoning map (official map) including district boundary lines and lot lines, as provided in this chapter.
(9) Hearing and deciding applications for variances from the development requirements of this chapter, but only in individual cases of practical difficulty or unnecessary hardship.
(10) Conducting such other business and affairs as may be, from time to time, designated by the board of commissioners.
(Ord. No. 006-95, 4-11-1995; Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. III, § 3-1.4)
706:
The planning and zoning board shall hear and decide appeals where it is alleged by the appellant that there is an error in any order, requirement, permit, decision or refusal made by the zoning administrator or other administrative official in the administration or enforcement of any provisions of this chapter. Such appeals shall be in accordance with this division.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-1)
707:
(a) An appeal to the planning and zoning board may be taken by any person, firm or corporation aggrieved or by any governmental officer, department, board or agency affected by any decision of the zoning administrator or other administrative official with respect to this chapter.
(b) Such appeal shall be made within 30 days following notification of the decision appealed from, by filing with the planning and zoning board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof. The zoning administrator shall forthwith transmit to the planning and zoning board all the papers constituting the record upon which the action was taken.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-1.1)
708:
(a) After receiving an application for an appeal, variance, or conditional use, the planning and zoning board shall schedule a public hearing.
(b) The application and fee determined by the county for a hearing and decision on requests for an appeal, variance, or conditional use shall be filed with the zoning administrator on forms provided by the county at least 30 days prior to the next scheduled planning and zoning board meeting. Each application shall contain such information as the zoning administrator may require to enable the planning and zoning board to make its decision on an appeal, conditional use, or variance request.
(c) The planning and zoning board shall publish once in a newspaper of general circulation in the county a written notice of such public hearing at least 15 days but not more than 45 days prior to the public hearing. The public notice shall indicate the time, place and nature of the appeal, variance or conditional use to be considered by the planning and zoning board. At the hearing any party may appear in person, or by agent, or by attorney.
(d) Additionally, at least 15 days before the scheduled public hearing, the zoning administrator shall post in a conspicuous place on the property a sign at least two feet by three feet in size. It shall set forth the time, place and purpose of the public hearing before the planning and zoning board. Acts of vandalism or natural occurrences limiting the effectiveness of notice by a sign posted on the property shall not invalidate any proceedings or action taken under this article.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-4)
709:
An appeal stays all actions by the zoning administrator seeking enforcement of or compliance with the order or decision appealed from, unless the zoning administrator certifies to the planning and zoning board that a stay would, in his opinion, cause imminent peril to life or property. In such case proceedings shall not be stayed otherwise than by a restraining order which may be granted by a court of competent jurisdiction.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-1.2)
710:
The appellant and any public agency or private individual shall be entitled to present evidence on matters before the planning and zoning board at the public hearing as required in this article.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-1.3)
711:
The planning and zoning board, in conformity with this chapter, may modify in whole or in part any order, requirement, or decision of the zoning administrator and to that end shall have the power of the zoning administrator or administrative official from whom the appeal is taken. The planning and zoning board may direct the issuance of a permit. It shall be the duty of the zoning administrator to carry out the decisions of the planning and zoning board.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-1.4)
714:
(a) The board of commissioners may from time to time, amend, supplement or change the regulations set forth in this chapter or the boundaries of the zoning districts established on the zoning map.
(b) No amendment shall become effective unless it shall have been initiated by either the board of commissioners or the planning and zoning board, the property owners, or an individual who has the owners' power of attorney authorizing him to act, or a request signed by 60 percent of the property owners who hold not less than 60 percent of the affected land.
(c) All proposed amendments shall first be submitted to the planning and zoning board, which shall conduct a public hearing and shall make a written recommendation to the board of commissioners. The power to approve and enact an amendment rests solely within the legislative discretion of the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-1(a), (b))
715:
As used in this article, the term "amendment" shall mean both a change to the official map and a change to the text of this chapter unless otherwise indicated.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-1(b))
716:
(a) All proposed amendments shall be initiated by an application with the zoning administrator on forms provided by the county. A standard fee shall be paid with the application in the amount of the advertising costs for the required public hearing. Application for amendment of these regulations may be in the form of a proposal for amendment of the text of regulations or a proposal for amendment of the zoning map.
(b) Within 15 days after receiving the application, the zoning administrator shall in writing inform the applicant of the date on which a public hearing will be held to consider the zoning change.
(c) No application will be accepted from any person regarding any property that is in violation of this chapter. If the property, at the time of application, which is the subject of an amendment or any other action of the board of commissioners, is found to be in violation of this chapter, then the board of commissioners will not accept or process any application from that applicant until the applicant voluntarily removes or changes the cause of the violation or ceases to be in violation. The applicant must then notify the zoning administrator that he is no longer in violation and obtain a release from the zoning administrator as to the violation. Once released, the board of commissioners will then accept the application for amendment of this chapter.
(d) Upon receiving an application for a map amendment and establishing the date of the public hearing concerning the petitioned request, the zoning administrator shall erect in a conspicuous place on the property in question or on the right-of-way of the nearest public road, if the property does not front a public road, a sign giving notice of both the existing zoning district in which the property is located and the requested change and the scheduled date and place for the public hearing.
(e) After acceptance of an application for amendment, the zoning administrator shall transmit a copy thereof to the planning and zoning board. The board will study the proposed amendment and determine if it meets the standards as enumerated in this division.
(f) Once the public hearing has been conducted in accordance with this division, the planning and zoning board shall make a written recommendation to the board of commissioners stating its approval or disapproval of the requested zoning change. Such recommendation shall be made by the planning and zoning board within 30 days of the public hearing or the requested zoning change shall be deemed to have been recommended for approval by the planning and zoning board.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-2)
718:
(a) Before making a written recommendation to the board of commissioners, the planning and zoning board shall hold a public hearing. The public hearing shall be conducted at the time and place specified by the planning and zoning board and as set forth in the public notice required in this division.
(b) The purpose of the hearing shall be to present to the public the proposed zoning amendment, and to receive comments thereon from the public.
(c) The board of commissioners shall consider the proceedings and comments of the hearing on the proposed zoning amendment in making a final decision on whether to approve or deny the amendment application.
(d) The planning and zoning board shall prescribe the rules of order for its deliberations on matters with which it is charged under this chapter, and said rules of order shall be consistent with the general requirements and purposes set forth in this chapter and state law concerning conduct of proceedings of public commissions, bodies and governmental units.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-4)
719:
At least 15, but not more than 45 days prior to the date set by the planning and zoning board for the hearing, a written notice shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the county setting forth the time, place, and purpose of the hearing. Such notice shall contain a summary of the proposed amendment, if a text amendment, and in the case of a map amendment, the location of the property, its area, name or owner, and the proposed change or classification. The cost of such newspaper notice shall be paid by the applicant for zoning amendment.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-5)
720:
(a) The public hearing shall be convened by the chairperson of the planning and zoning board at the time and place scheduled.
(b) The chairperson shall open any hearing with an explanation of the purpose of the hearing and a description of the general rules for the conduct of the hearing. The chairperson or his delegate may describe the authority and role of the planning and zoning board in any zoning decision.
(c) The chairperson shall review the procedures for holding the public hearing which shall be as follows:
(1) No person may speak until recognized by the chairperson. Upon rising to speak, the person recognized must first state his name and address.
(2) The person speaking will be allowed two minutes to express opinions and make points on each separate element of the proposed zoning revisions which he wishes to address; provided, however, that no person shall speak longer than an aggregate of ten minutes.
(3) Any remark amounting to an attack on the character or personal integrity of another individual, or a comment not factually supportable, or a comment in the form of an emotional outburst, shall be not germane to the purpose of any hearing and may be ruled out of order.
(4) Additional persons will be recognized in accordance with the procedure set forth above for the purpose of addressing additional issues and making additional points, but no speaker shall be allowed to address points which have already been thoroughly discussed.
(5) In the case of each petition for amendment to the zoning regulations, the chairperson shall allow the applicant or the agent for the applicant, to speak first and to present the arguments of the applicant in favor of the proposed amendment.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-6)
721:
(a) Once the planning and zoning board submits a written recommendation to the board of commissioners, the board of commissioners, at a regular meeting, may take action approving or rejecting the proposal at that meeting, or the board of commissioners may table the question for consideration at its next regular meeting or a called meeting to be held no later than the next regular meeting.
(b) The planning and zoning board's role in any zoning decision shall be advisory only. Any zoning decision shall be made by the board of commissioners who shall either approve or disapprove the proposed zoning amendment.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-7)
722:
Appeals from the decision of the board of commissioners regarding the approval or disapproval of a zoning amendment shall be made in accordance with the judicial review provisions in section 20-33.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-8)
723:
No application for amendment of the zoning chapter once heard by the planning and zoning board shall be accepted for a rehearing until at least six months shall have passed since written recommendation was made by the planning and zoning board to the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-9)
724:
An application may not be withdrawn or amended by the applicant after the public hearing has been advertised, unless the planning and zoning board by a majority vote allow an application to be withdrawn without prejudice.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XXI, § 21-10)
727:
(a) Except as otherwise provided, no structure or land shall, after the adoption of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived, be used and no structure or part thereof shall be erected, altered or moved unless in conformity with the requirements herein specified for the district in which it is located.
(b) The county shall not accept any subdivision not designed, developed and recorded in accordance with the provisions of these regulations, nor shall it improve, maintain, grade or pave any street within such subdivision unless such street shall have met the specifications described herein.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-1.1, art. XIII, § 13-5(c))
728:
No land shall be subdivided, sold, or transferred for development until each of the following conditions has occurred in accordance with this chapter:
(1) The developer or his agent has submitted the required fees, plats and plans as described in these regulations to the zoning administrator;
(2) Obtained approval of all these plats and plans, including approval of the final plat or plan by the planning and zoning board; and
(3) The approved final plat is recorded with the county clerk of superior court.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-1.2)
729:
No lot, street, alley, improvement, easement, right-of-way or other property or property right of any kind shall be conveyed, by deed or otherwise, to the county, the governing authority or other public authority without its express acceptance of such conveyance as indicated by the signature of its authorized agent on such deed or other document of conveyance.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-5(d))
730:
The county shall not authorize the extension of water service, sewer service, or other publicly operated services of any subdivision not designed, developed and recorded in accordance with the provisions of these regulations or the extension of utility services to any parcel created in violation of these regulations.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-5(e))
731:
Except as hereinafter provided, no building or structure shall be erected on a lot unless such building or structure, enlargement, additions or alterations conform to the area regulations and setback requirements of the zone in which it is located.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-2)
732:
No lot shall be reduced, diminished and so maintained that the yards, other open space or total lot area shall be smaller than prescribed by this chapter, nor shall the density of population be increased in any manner except in conformity with the regulations herein established.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-3)
733:
No required yard or other open space around an existing building, or which is hereafter provided around any building for the purpose of complying with the provisions of this chapter, shall be considered as providing a yard or open space for any other building; nor shall any yard or other required open space on an adjoining lot be considered as providing a yard or open space on a lot whereon a building is to be erected.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-4)
734:
Every building hereafter erected or structurally altered shall be located on a lot, and in no case shall there be more than one principal building and the customary accessory buildings on one lot of land. However, in the R-A district a second principal residential building shall be allowed on a lot provided that the lot has a minimum area of 80,000 square feet and that the second principal building is located no closer than 100 linear feet from the first principal building.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-5)
735:
No sign, construction, structure, fence, wall, hedge, bush, outdoor use or other obstruction to a clear view which extends over three feet in height shall be permitted at any corner of intersecting streets and a straight line connecting them at points 25 feet distant from the intersection of the street lines.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-6)
736:
At each end of a double frontage lot there shall be a front yard of the depth required by this chapter for the zone in which each street frontage is located; provided, that one of the front yards may serve as a rear yard.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-7)
737:
All land physically unsuitable for subdivision shall not be improved. This includes: property affected by flooding, bad drainage, steep slopes, rock formations, or other such features which may endanger health, life or property, aggravate erosion, increase flood hazard, or necessitate excessive expenditures of public funds for supply or maintenance of services.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-8)
738:
Parcels that are combined or uncombined as shown on the official tax appraisal map shall not be resubdivided except in conformance with all provisions of these regulations.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-9)
739:
(a) If a proposed subdivision includes land that is zoned for commercial or industrial purposes, the layout of the subdivision with respect to the land shall make provision as the planning and zoning board may require. Site plan approval and nonresidential subdivision plat approval may proceed simultaneously at the discretion of the planning and zoning board.
(b) A nonresidential subdivision shall be subject to all the requirements of these regulations, as well as such additional standards required by the planning and zoning board, and shall conform to the proposed land use and standards established in the comprehensive plan.
(c) In addition to the principles and standards in these regulations, which are appropriate to the planning of all subdivisions, the applicant shall demonstrate to the satisfaction of the planning and zoning board that the street, parcel, and block pattern proposed is specifically adapted to the uses anticipated and takes into account other uses in the vicinity. The following principles and standards shall be observed:
(1) All proposed industrial parcels shall be suitable in area and dimension to the types of industrial development anticipated.
(2) Street rights-of-way and pavement shall be adequate to accommodate the type and volume of traffic anticipated to be generated thereupon.
(3) Special requirements may be imposed by the county with respect to street, curb, gutter, and sidewalk design and construction.
(4) Special requirements may be imposed by the county with respect to the installation of public utilities, including water, sewer, and stormwater drainage.
(5) Every effort shall be made to protect adjacent residential areas from potential nuisance from a proposed commercial or industrial subdivision, including the provision of extra depth in parcels backing up on existing or potential residential development and provisions for a permanently landscaped buffer strip as per article XV, division 4 of this chapter.
(6) Streets carrying nonresidential traffic, especially truck traffic, shall not normally be extended to the boundaries of adjacent existing or potential residential areas.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, §§ 4-10.1, 4-10.2)
740:
A subdivision plat that represents four lots or less fronting on a public or private road shall not be subject to the required improvements of sections 20-390 and 20-392 and the design standards specified in article VII of this chapter, if it meets the following conditions:
(1) The original tract for subdivision fronts for a distance of 150 feet on a public or private road which is identified as such on the official county road map, as adopted by the board of commissioners.
(2) The size and zoning classification of each lot resulting from the subdivision meets the minimum standards set forth in this chapter.
(3) Platted lots on streets and roads which have been accepted as part of established subdivisions under the minimum standards of this chapter cannot be further subdivided unless such future subdivision was made part of the original approval of the plat of such subdivision.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IV, § 4-11)
741:
Reasonable fees shall be paid along with the application for approval of a preliminary plat or final plat. The amount of the fees charged shall be as set forth by the board of commissioners. The schedule of fees shall be posted in the office of the zoning administrator and may be altered or amended only by the board of commissioners. Until all applicable fees have been paid in full, no action shall be taken on any application or appeal. Fees will be assessed and shall be charged to applicants to cover the cost of administration, inspection, publication of notice and similar matters for rezoning applications, appeals, conditional use permits, variance applications, subdivision plat approval, sign permits and other administrative relief.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-6)
742:
The following are excluded from the subdivision requirements of this chapter:
(1) The combination or recombination of portions of previously platted lots where the total number of lots is not increased and the resultant lots comply with the standards set forth in these regulations and all other ordinances of the county.
(2) The division of land into five or fewer parcels which front onto public streets and where the resultant lots conform to this chapter, provided that approval is secured from the health department in cases where septic tanks are intended to be utilized or other proper authority if central sewage disposal is intended to be utilized. Exemptions under this provision shall be verified and indicated on the plat by the zoning administrator.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XVIII, § 18-6(d))
745:
The owner of any land lying within the area of jurisdiction of these regulations who wishes to subdivide such land shall seek approval by the planning and zoning board according to the procedures set forth in this article.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. V, § 5-1)
746:
(a) For purposes of this section the term "official submission date" means the day on which the statutory period required for formal approval, conditional approval or disapproval of a preliminary or final plat begins.
(b) The official submission date of a preliminary plat shall be the date of the finalization of the hearing thereon before the planning and zoning board.
(c) The official submission date of a final subdivision plat shall be the date of the finalization and closure of the public meeting thereon.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. V, § 5-1)
747:
(a) Prior to the review, consideration and approval of a preliminary plat by the planning and zoning board, the subdivider may schedule an initial meeting with the zoning administrator to discuss the proposed development. The developer may offer a simple sketch plan showing existing conditions within the site and in its vicinity and the proposed layout and development of the subdivision to the zoning administrator for comments if desired.
(b) The purpose of the meeting is to assist the subdivider with questions he may have prior to extensive site planning necessary for the preparation of the preliminary plat and to enable the subdivider to become familiar with the regulations affecting the land to be subdivided.
(c) Recommendations received from the zoning administrator concerning the proposed development or the sketch plan do not authorize the developer to begin the proposed construction or improvements.
(d) No fee shall be charged for this informal consultation and no formal application shall be required.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. V, § 5-2)
748:
Prior to making any street improvements or installing any utilities, the prospective subdivider shall submit to the planning and zoning board a preliminary plat as specified in article V of this chapter. Approval of the preliminary plat by the planning and zoning board constitutes authorization for the subdivider to develop the subdivision subject to the minimum standards for required improvements prescribed in sections 20-390 and 20-392, and the minimum design standards prescribed in article VII of this chapter.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. V, § 5-3)
749:
After approval of the preliminary plat, the subdivider may proceed with the preparation of the final plat and other documents as may be required in connection therewith. No final plat shall be approved by the planning and zoning board until either:
(1) The required improvements listed are constructed in satisfactory manner and approved by the zoning administrator and the planning and zoning board; or
(2) In lieu of such prior construction, the planning and zoning board has received written notification from the county attorney that the board of commissioners has accepted an approved bond or security in the amount equal to the estimated cost of installation and completion of the required improvements, whereby improvements may be made and utilities installed without cost to the county in the event of default by the subdivider.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. V, § 5-4)
750:
Upon approval of a final plat, the subdivider shall submit to the planning and zoning board for its approval a plat of record prepared in accordance with this chapter.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. V, § 5-5)
754:
(a) The subdivider shall submit to the planning and zoning board, at least 30 days prior to the next regular meeting of the planning and zoning board, the following:
(1) A letter requesting review and approval of a preliminary plat giving the name and address of a person to whom the notice of the hearing by the planning and zoning board on the preliminary plat shall be sent.
(2) Five copies of a preliminary plat of the proposed subdivision drawn to a scale not less than one inch equals 100 feet.
(3) A subdivision review and inspection fee as determined by the board of commissioners.
(b) The planning and zoning board shall not accept the fee until completion of the application and the requirements of this section are carried out.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-1)
755:
Upon receipt of a formal application for preliminary plat approval and all accompanying material, the planning and zoning board shall call a public hearing for the next scheduled meeting of the planning and zoning board to be held at least 30 days after the date of the application.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-12)
756:
(a) Public notice of the hearing on the application for preliminary plat approval shall be given, at least 15 but not more than 45 days, prior to the scheduled public hearing.
(b) The zoning administrator shall file a notice of public hearing which shall be published in the newspaper of general circulation in the county setting forth the time, place, and purpose of the hearing. Such notice shall identify the property affected. The cost of such newspaper notice shall be paid by the applicant for preliminary plat approval.
(c) At least 15 days before the scheduled public hearing, the zoning administrator shall post, in a conspicuous place on the property, a sign at least two feet by three feet in size. It shall set forth the time, place and purpose of the public hearing before the planning and zoning board.
(d) Additionally, notice of the time and place of the hearing shall be sent by the zoning administrator by registered or certified mail to the applicant for preliminary plat approval, not less than five days prior to the date of the hearing.
(e) Acts of vandalism or natural occurrences limiting the effectiveness of notice by a sign posted on the property shall not invalidate any proceedings or action taken under this article.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-3)
757:
(a) The planning and zoning board shall approve, disapprove, or approve with modification, the preliminary plat within 60 days after the date it is presented at the public hearing. If disapproved, a notation of the planning and zoning board's action shall be made on two copies of the preliminary plat, including a statement of the reasons for disapproval. One copy will be returned to the subdivider or his agent, and one copy retained by the planning and zoning board.
(b) Preliminary approval of the subdivision plat shall be noted on the plat and certified by the planning and zoning board. Also noted shall be the date on which the planning and zoning board granted preliminary approval and the date of written notification to the subdivider or subdivider's authorized agent.
(c) Unless the subdivider agrees in writing to an extension of the time limitation in this section, failure of the planning and zoning board to act with 60 days from the finalization of the public hearing regarding the preliminary plat shall constitute approval thereof and a certificate of approval shall be issued by the board on demand.
(d) Approval of a preliminary subdivision plat shall not constitute approval of the final subdivision plat. It only indicates approval of the layout as a guide to the preparation of the final plat.
(e) Approval of the preliminary plat by the planning and zoning board constitutes authorization for the subdivider to proceed to comply with the other requirements of these regulations and the preparation of the final subdivision plat subject to the minimum standards prescribed in these regulations. However, the subdivider, subdivision owner, or agent of the subdivider or owner shall not transfer, sell, agree to sell, or negotiate to sell any part of the subdivision by reference or exhibition until after the planning and zoning board has approved the final plat and the applicant has filed the plat of record with the clerk of the county superior court.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-4)
759:
The planning and zoning board may require that all public improvements be installed and dedicated prior to the signing of the final subdivision plat. The planning and zoning board shall require the applicant to indicate on the plat all roads and public utility improvements which shall be required to be established or extended, and any other special requirements deemed necessary by the planning and zoning board in order to conform the subdivision plat to the county comprehensive plan.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-6)
760:
The approval of a preliminary plat shall be effective for a period of one year from the date that the preliminary plat is approved by the planning and zoning board, at the end of which time the applicant must have submitted a final subdivision plat for approval. If a subdivision plat is not submitted for final approval within the one-year period, the preliminary approval shall be null and void, and the applicant shall be required to submit a new plat for preliminary plat review subject to the then-existing zoning restrictions and subdivision regulations.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-7)
763:
The preliminary plat shall be drawn to a scale of not less than one inch equals 100 feet and meet the minimum standards of design set forth in these regulations and shall include the following information:
(1) Full name, location and acreage of proposed subdivision.
(2) Name, address, and telephone number of owner of record and subdivider, and architect, surveyor, engineer or designer.
(3) All names and addresses of adjoining subdivisions or all deed record owners of the land adjacent to the site.
(4) Date, scale, and north arrow on map.
(5) Total number of lots and average lot size.
(6) Location or vicinity map at a scale of not less than one inch equals one mile tying the subdivision into the present road system and relating the subdivision to its surrounding area.
(7) A written legal description (metes and bounds with all bearing and distances) of the acreage to be subdivided.
(8) Proper identification of the boundaries of the tract to be subdivided with all bearings and distances indicated. The boundary survey shall be to such a degree of accuracy that the error of closure is 1:7,500 or greater.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-8.1)
764:
The preliminary plat shall include the following existing conditions:
(1) Topographic map on a scale of one inch representing 100 feet or less and contour intervals of five feet or less, showing major watercourses, marshes, rock outcrops, wooded areas, and other outstanding features.
(2) Zoning district classification of land to be subdivided and adjoining land (if applicable).
(3) In case of resubdivision, a copy of the existing plat with proposed resubdivision superimposed thereon.
(4) Location of natural features such as streams, lakes, swamps, and land subject to flood based on a 100-year flood frequency on the property to be subdivided.
(5) Location of existing adjoining property lines and existing buildings on the property to be subdivided.
(6) Location and right-of-way of streets, roads, railroads and utility lines either on or adjacent to the property to be subdivided, specifying whether utility lines are in easements or right-of-way and showing the location of poles or towers.
(7) Size and location of existing sewers, water mains, drains, culverts or other underground facilities within the street or within the right-of-way of streets or roads adjoining the tract. Grades and invert elevations of sewers shall be shown.
(8) The acreage of each drainage area affecting the proposed subdivision.
(9) All elevations shall refer to mean sea level datum where public water or public sewers are to be installed.
(10) Location of city limit lines and county lines (if applicable).
(11) Location of any wetlands situated on the property to be subdivided.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-8.2)
765:
The preliminary plat shall include the following proposed conditions:
(1) Layout of streets, roads, alleys, public crosswalks, with widths, road names, or designations, grades and cross sections.
(2) Profile of proposed streets showing natural and finished grades with percent of grade slope.
(3) Detailed layout of all lots, including building setback lines, scaled dimensions on lots, utility easements with width and use.
(4) Construction drawings of sanitary sewers (if applicable) with grade, pipe size, location of manholes, and points of discharge and percolation tests, soil borings and wells as specified by the health department.
(5) Construction drawings of storm sewer system with grade, pipe size, and location of outlet. Storm sewers shall be sized to accommodate runoff from a ten-year frequency rainfall.
