(6) Plans of all drainage provisions, retaining walls, curbing, planting, anti-erosion devices or other protective devices to be constructed in connection with, or as a part of the proposed work, together with a map showing the drainage area of land tributary to the site and estimated runoff of the area served by any drains.
(7) Construction drawings of water supply system with pipe size and location of hydrants and valves.
(8) Designation of all land (if any) to be reserved or dedicated for public use.
(9) Designation of proposed use of all lots to be used for other than single-family residential (if any).
(10) Proposed major contour changes to areas where substantial cut or fill is to be done.
(11) A timing schedule indicating the anticipated starting and completion dates of the development sequence and the time of exposure of each area prior to the completion of effective erosion and sediment control measures.
(12) Total number of lots, total acreage, total length and width of new streets.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-8.3)
766:
A certificate of approval of the preliminary plat by the planning and zoning board shall be inscribed on the plat as follows:
Pursuant to county land use and development regulations, all the requirements for approval have been fulfilled. This preliminary plat was given preliminary approval by the county planning and zoning board on ___________, 20___.
This preliminary approval does not constitute approval of a final plat. This certificate of approval shall expire and be null and void on ___________, 20___.
_____ Chairperson Planning and Zoning Board |
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VI, § 6-9)
769:
The final subdivision plat shall be prepared in accordance with the standards set forth in this article and O.C.G.A. title 15, ch. 6, art. 2 (O.C.G.A. § 15-6-50 et seq.).
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-1)
770:
After the preliminary plat of a proposed land subdivision has been given approval by the planning and zoning board, the subdivider may, within one year from the date of such approval, submit to the planning and zoning board an original and two duplicate copies of the final subdivision plat application prepared in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, together with two Mylar sepias.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-1.1(a))
771:
The zoning administrator shall check the final plat application for conformance with the approved preliminary plat and with the provisions of this chapter. Each plat shall contain, in such language as prescribed by the planning and zoning board, a certificate by the surveyor as to survey and platting requirements; a certificate by the engineer as to engineering requirements; a certificate as to floor elevation as related to the sanitary sewer system; a certification of acceptance by the planning and zoning board; and if approved, a certificate of final plat approval by the planning and zoning board.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-1.1(b))
772:
The application for final plat approval shall be accompanied by a certificate by the owner as to ownership and all formal irrevocable offers of dedication to the public of streets, easements, utilities, parks, and open spaces. For purposes hereof, authentication shall be in the certificate of ownership and dedication form as provided in section 20-297.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-1.1(c))
773:
The applicant shall deliver a full covenant and warranty deed to all dedicated lands and improvements in proper form for recording, together with any requirement deemed necessary by the county attorney before he shall sign the final subdivision plat.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-1.1(d))
775:
The following signed certificates shall appear on the final plat which is submitted to the planning and zoning board by the subdivider:
(1) Certificate of approval for recording. (To be placed on an original of the approved final plat by the planning and zoning board and returned to the subdivider for recording.)
The subdivision plat known as ___________ has been found to comply with the county land use and development regulations and was approved by the planning and zoning board on the ___ day of ___________, 20___, for the recording in the office of the clerk of the Superior Court of Jefferson County, Georgia.
Jefferson County Planning and Zoning Board |
_____ Chairperson |
(2) Certificate of accuracy.
I hereby certify that this plat is a true, correct and accurate survey as required by the county land use and development regulations and was prepared from an actual survey of the property made under my supervision, and that monuments shown have been located and placed to the specifications set forth in said regulations.
By: _____ (Registered Land Surveyor Signature) |
_____ (Typed Name) |
(Surveyor's Seal Required) |
Registered Land Surveyor No. _____ |
Date: _____ |
(3) Certificate of ownership and dedication, individuals.
It is hereby certified that I am (we are) the owners of the property shown and described hereon and that I (we) hereby irrevocably dedicate all streets, alleys, walks, parks and other sites to public or private use as noted. It is further certified that the streets, drainage system, sewer system and water system in ___________ Subdivision as shown on the plat dated ________ prepared by ___________ have (has) been installed in accordance with the preliminary plat (construction drawings) approved (date) ________. It is understood this is not an assumption of maintenance by the governing authority. This dedication is for the public's right of ingress and egress only.
_____ Date | (Owner) _____ Printed Name (and Address)
(Witness) _____ Printed Name | (Owner) _____ Printed Name (and Address)
(Witness) _____ Printed Name |
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-5(q))
776:
(a) The planning and zoning board shall schedule the final subdivision plat determination for its next available regular meeting agenda. Public notice of final plat determination shall be given at least 15, but not more than 45 days prior to the next available regular meeting. The zoning administrator shall file a written notice which shall be published in the newspaper of general circulation in the county setting forth the time, place, and purpose of the meeting. Such notice shall identify the property affected. The cost of such newspaper notice shall be paid by the applicant for final plat approval.
(b) At the meeting, the planning and zoning board shall approve, disapprove, or approve with modification, the final plat. A notation of the action shall be made on the original and duplicate plats and one Mylar sepia of the final plat, including a statement of the reasons therefor if the final plat is disapproved.
(c) If action on the final plat is not taken by the planning and zoning board within 60 days of the date of submittal, the final plat shall be considered approved and a certificate of approval shall be issued on demand. However, the applicant for approval may waive this requirement and consent to an extension of time.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-2)
777:
No plat of a subdivision within the county shall be filed or recorded by the clerk of the county superior court until the final plat shall have been prepared, submitted to, approved and recorded according to these regulations.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-5(b))
778:
(a) After approval of the final subdivision plat by the planning and zoning board, the plat shall be filed for record in the office of the clerk of the county superior court.
(b) The clerk of the superior court shall not accept for record or file any plat which has not been prepared in accordance with the provisions of this chapter and which has not been stamped approved by the planning and zoning board. For purposes hereof, authentication shall be in the certificate of approval for recording form as provided in section 20-297.
(c) One blueprint, shall be filed with the clerk of superior court who shall enter thereon the filing date. One Mylar copy shall be delivered to the planning and zoning board as required. One copy of all deeds and plats with recording information shall be delivered to the tax assessor's office.
(d) Any person requesting a copy of the recorded plat shall include an extra blueprint copy at the time of filing for record.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-3)
779:
The approval of a plat does not constitute acceptance by the county of the offer of dedication of any streets, sidewalks, parks or other public facilities shown on a plat.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-4)
783:
The design standards contained in this article shall apply to all new development and they shall conform to the minimum requirements of the property's zoning designation as required in this chapter.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-1)
784:
The name of each subdivision must have the approval of the planning and zoning board. The name shall not duplicate nor closely approximate the name of an existing subdivision.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-5)
785:
In accordance with this chapter, the adequate provision of fire hydrants necessitates that:
(1) Every development subdivided or unsubdivided that is served by a public water system shall include a system of fire hydrants sufficient to provide adequate fire protection for the buildings located or intended to be located within such development.
(2) Water lines that serve hydrants shall be at least six-inch lines, and, unless no other practicable alternative is available, no such line shall be dead-end lines.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-5(r))
786:
Wherever grading or filling occurs on lots within the subdivision, the subdivider shall first stockpile the topsoil from the affected areas immediately after grading and filling and shall redistribute to areas of disturbed soil sufficient topsoil to support growth of lawn grass, and other vegetation and shall immediately seed such areas with appropriate vegetative cover to prevent erosion, silting of streams, and other damages. Due regard shall be shown for such desirable trees as are already on the site, and grading and filling should be planned to preserve as many as possible.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-5(t))
787:
The planning and zoning board shall not approve a subdivision where the soil conditions have been determined not suitable for development by the county health department pursuant to local, state, and federal laws, regulations and standards.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-6)
788:
(a) Length. Blocks shall be neither less than 400 feet nor more than 1,200 feet in length, except as the planning and zoning board considers necessary to secure efficient use of land or desired features of street pattern. In blocks greater than 800 feet in length, the planning and zoning board may require at locations it deems necessary one or more public crosswalks of not less than ten feet in width to extend entirely across the block, or pedestrian easements in lieu thereof.
(b) Width. Blocks shall be wide enough to allow two rows of lots, except where reverse frontage on major streets is provided or when prevented by topographic conditions or size of property or location next to an arterial road, in which case the planning and zoning board may approve a single row of lots.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-3)
789:
Except where alleys or rear service drives are permitted for the purpose, easements along rear or side lot lines shall be at least 15 feet wide and shall be required for the extension of existing or planned utilities.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-4(a))
792:
In cases in which a subdivision is traversed by a stream or drainage channel, there shall be provided a stormwater easement of such width along each side of the stream as the planning and zoning board deems necessary for the purpose of widening, deepening, protecting, relocating, or otherwise improving such drainage element. Additional requirements include:
(1) A five-foot easement along all side property lines.
(2) A ten-foot easement along all rear property lines.
(3) All storm drainage pipes shall be located within a ten-foot easement.
(4) All stormwater discharge into natural drainage areas shall be as straight as possible.
(5) All storm drainage pipes shall be at least 18 inches in diameter and 18 inches below the surface and shall have a slope of at least one percent.
(6) Catchbasins shall be located at all low points of streets and shall be located so as to service no more than four acres.
(7) High-water elevation contour based on a 25-year storm at the entrance of each head wall.
(8) All drainage easements, natural ditches, and drainage areas shall be grassed or rip-rapped as necessary to control erosion.
(9) All subdivisions plans shall include a method of control so as to prevent the silting or erosion of natural drainage areas, natural drains and streams, and adjoining property; such plans shall also provide for control of the rate of discharge of excess water.
(10) In addition to the requirements of these regulations, all property located in a floodprone area shall be developed in accordance with the minimum state and federal standards governing floodprone areas.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-4(b))
795:
After the adoption of a major street plan as provided by law, the county or other public authority shall not accept, lay out, open, improve, grade, pave or light any street or authorize the laying of water mains, sewers, connections or other facilities or utilities in any street within the territorial jurisdiction of the county unless such street has been accepted or opened as, or shall otherwise have received the legal status of, a public street prior to the attachment of the county's jurisdiction, or unless such street corresponds in its location and lines with a street shown on a subdivision plat duly approved by the planning and zoning board.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 8-3)
796:
(a) At the preliminary plat stage, the planning and zoning board may limit the number of entrances, driveways, or curb cuts.
(b) At the preliminary and final plat stages, the planning and zoning board shall be consistent with all state, federal, and local laws and applicable ordinances, including the state department of transportation rules and all amendments or revisions in effect as of the date of the preliminary plat approval.
(c) At the preliminary plat stage, the planning and zoning board may consider safety as well as require available alternatives for reducing the number of entrances, driveways or curb cuts.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-5(u))
797:
The planning and zoning board shall not approve a subdivision in a location where the existing roads providing primary access are inadequate to serve the additional traffic generated by the development. If the ditches on existing county streets are to be used for drainage from the subdivision, the developer will re-grade said ditches and provide an all-weather drainage outlet. All re-grading and drainage outlets shall be approved by the board of commissioners or its authorized representatives.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 8-4)
798:
Street name signs shall be installed at all intersections within a subdivision. The location and design shall be approved by the planning and zoning board.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. VII, § 7-5(s))
799:
In order to provide for streets of suitable location, width and improvements to accommodate prospective traffic and afford satisfactory access to fire, police and sanitation department personnel as well as road maintenance equipment, and to coordinate streets so as to compose a convenient system and avoid hardships to adjoining property, the design standards in this article for streets are hereby required and shall be planned for and provided by the subdivider, prior to final plat approval. Streets shall conform to current county road construction and maintenance specifications.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2)
800:
Streets and roads are hereby classified according to the function which they are to serve, the type, speed, and volume of traffic they will carry, and the required standards of design. The classifications of streets and roads shall be arterial roads, collector streets, and local streets; and are displayed on the major road plan adopted by the planning and zoning board. The designation in the major road plan of arterials and collectors shall not prevent other streets proposed in or adjoining subdivisions from being similarly classified. Street classifications and subclassifications are as follows:
(1) Arterial roads or streets.
(2) Collector streets.
(3) Local streets.
a. Residential:
1. Small lot subdivisions (lots less than 50,000 square feet).
2. Large lot subdivisions (lots larger than 50,000 square feet with a minimum frontage of 125 lineal feet).
3. Rural subdivisions (lots larger than 2.5 acres).
4. Large lot rural subdivisions (lots larger than 5.0 acres).
b. Industrial.
c. Commercial.
d. Service drive.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.1)
801:
(a) The location and width of all streets and roads shall conform to the official major road plan as adopted by the planning and zoning board.
(b) Existing streets which terminate at or adjoin a subdivision boundary shall be deemed a part of the subdivision. The proposed street system within a subdivision shall have the right-of-way of existing streets extended no less than the required minimum width. Subdivisions that adjoin only one side of existing streets shall dedicate one-half of the additional right-of-way needed to meet minimum width requirements. If any part of the subdivision includes both sides of an existing street all the required additional right-of-way shall be dedicated.
(c) The proposed street layout shall be coordinated with the street system of the surrounding area. Where possible, existing major streets shall be extended.
(d) Where, in the opinion of the planning and zoning board it is necessary to provide for street access to adjoining property, proposed streets shall be extended by dedication of right-of-way to the boundary of such property.
(e) When an arterial road adjoins or is included in a subdivision, lots therein which abut the arterial road shall be provided with another means of access, e.g. platting a single tier of lots which back to the arterial road and front on a minor street, platting a service drive, platting a looped land service street and culs-de-sac, platting a rear service drive for access, or other methods approved by the planning and zoning board. Subdivision streets which intersect an arterial road shall do so at intervals not less 1,200 feet for limited access arterial roads and 400 feet for other arterial roads.
(f) When land is subdivided into parcels larger than ordinary building lots, such parcels shall be arranged so as to allow for the opening of streets in the future.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.2)
802:
Proposed streets which are obviously in alignment with other existing and named streets shall bear the assigned name of the existing streets. In no case shall the name of the proposed streets duplicate or be phonetically similar to existing street names, regardless of the use of suffix, street, avenue, boulevard, drive, place, court, etc. It shall be unlawful for any person in laying out any new street or road to name such street or road on any plat by marking, or in any deed or instrument, without first getting approval of the planning and zoning board.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.3)
803:
Street jogs with centerline offsets by less than the minimum stopping distance specified in this division shall be prohibited.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.4)
804:
Street intersections shall be as nearly at right angles as practicable.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.5)
805:
A cul-de-sac is a minor street and is not to extend more than 700 feet in length. Such street shall be provided with a turnaround having a roadway diameter of at least 80 feet and a right-of-way diameter of at least 100 feet.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.6)
806:
Service alleys or drives may be required in multiple dwelling, commercial, and industrial developments and shall have a minimum surface treatment width of 15 feet, but shall not be provided in one- and two-family residential developments unless the subdivider provides evidence satisfactory to the planning and zoning board of the need for alleys.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.7)
808:
When a subdivision is proposed with frontage along an existing arterial road, or state numbered highway, every attempt must be made to provide an access road or frontage road for direct access to the proposed lots. The planning and zoning board shall evaluate this requirement in an attempt to reduce the number and frequency of curb cuts along arterial roads and state numbered highways.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.9)

810:

(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.11)

812:
(a) Where a deflection angle of more than ten degrees in the alignment of a street occurs, the radius of curvature of the centerline of said street shall be not less than as follows:

(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. IX, § 9-2.12)
815:
Improvement guarantees shall be provided to ensure the proper installation and maintenance of required streets, utility and other improvements. The nature and duration of the guarantee shall be structured to achieve this goal without adding unnecessary costs to the developer of a proposed subdivision.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. X, § 10-1)
816:
(a) Before recording the final plat, or as a condition of final site plan approval, the planning and zoning board may require and shall accept in accordance with the requirements of this chapter the following guarantees:
(1) The furnishing of a performance guarantee in an amount not to exceed 120 percent of the cost of installation of improvements;
(2) The provision for a maintenance guarantee for a period not to exceed two years after final acceptance of the improvement, in an amount not to exceed 15 percent of the cost of the improvement. In the event that other governmental agencies or public utilities automatically will own the utilities to be installed, or the improvements are covered by a performance guarantee or maintenance guarantee to another governmental agency, no performance guarantee or maintenance guarantee shall be required by the planning and zoning board for such utilities or improvements.
(b) The time allowed for installation of the improvements for which the performance guarantee has been provided may be extended by the planning and zoning board by resolution.
(c) Upon substantial completion of all required improvements, the developer may notify the planning and zoning board in writing of the completion or substantial completion of improvement and it shall send a copy to the building inspector. The building inspector shall inspect all improvements of which such notice has been given and shall file a detailed report, in writing with the planning and zoning board indicating either approval, partial approval or rejection of such improvements with a statement of reasons for any rejection. The cost of the improvements as approved or rejected shall be set forth.
(d) The planning and zoning board shall either approve, partially approve, or reject the improvements on the basis of the report of the building inspector and it shall notify the developer in writing of the contents of the report and the action not later than 30 days after receipt of the notice from the developer of the completion of the improvements. Failure of the planning and zoning board to provide notification within 30 days after receipt of the notice from the developer of the completion of the improvements shall be held to constitute approval of the improvement and the obligor as well as the surety, if any, shall be released from all liability pursuant to such performance guarantee for such improvements.
(e) Where partial approval is granted, the developer shall be released from all liability except for that portion of improvements not yet approved.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. X, § 10-2)
817:
The performance and maintenance guarantees shall be provided by a variety of means including, but not limited to the following:
(1) Security bond. The applicant may obtain a security bond from a surety bonding company authorized to do business in this state.
(2) Letter of credit. The applicant may provide an irrevocable letter of credit from a bank.
(3) Escrow account. The applicant shall deposit cash or other instruments readily convertible into cash at face value, either with the county, or in escrow with a bank.
(4) Subdivision improvement agreement. An applicant may provide as a guarantee a Subdivision Improvement Agreement between the lender, applicant and the county.
(5) Cash bond. A cash bond in the amount of $1,000.00 will be required of all timber harvesting operators using county-maintained roads.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. X, § 10-3)
820:
No construction activity of any kind, including grading, installation of improvements, and building, shall begin on any land subject to these regulations without prior approval of the preliminary plat by the planning and zoning board.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XI, § 11-1)
821:
The grading operations may begin following approval of the preliminary plat.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XI, § 11-2)
822:
Utility installation shall not occur until the zoning administrator has approved the rough grade of the street and shoulder preparation.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XI, § 11-3)
823:
Periodic inspection during the installation of the physical improvements in a subdivision shall be made by the zoning administrator to ensure conformity with the approved plans and specifications. The subdivider shall notify the zoning administrator when each phase of the installation is completed and ready for inspection.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XI, § 11-4)
824:
No lot or parcel of land shall be sold or transferred or a building permit issued until the final plat, of which said lot or parcel is a part, shall have been approved and recorded as provided for in these regulations.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XI, § 11-5)
825:
The zoning administrator or building inspector shall not issue any permit for the erection of any building or structure to be located in any subdivision, of which a plat is required to be recorded pursuant to the provisions of these regulations, until such plat shall have been admitted to record as provided for in these regulations.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XI, § 11-6)
826:
No dwelling within the county may be occupied for dwelling purposes until all required utility installations, including water supply and sanitary sewer systems, have been completed to the satisfaction of the planning and zoning board.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XI, § 11-7)
829:
Some zoning districts permit certain uses only upon approval of the planning and zoning board. These uses are identified in this chapter as conditional uses and such uses may be allowed under special conditions. The granting of a conditional use does not constitute a permanent change in zoning or use. The conditional use may be forfeited if it does not meet the criteria provided in this article. Generally, a conditional use shall be compatible with the applicable zoning district under special conditions.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-2)
830:
Conditional uses shall be permitted subject to an approval by the planning and zoning board according to procedures established in this chapter. The required review shall determine whether the uses conform to the standards set forth in this article.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-2(a))
831:
The conditional use shall be approved if it meets all the following factors:
(1) A rezoning to a more intensive zoning district, which contains that use as a use by right, would not be appropriate for the property.
(2) The location and character of the conditional use shall be compatible with the community development pattern and consistent with the needs of the neighborhood.
(3) The conditional use will not be injurious to the use and enjoyment of the natural environment or of other property in the immediate vicinity, or diminish and impair property values within the surrounding neighborhood.
(4) The conditional use will not increase state or local expenditures in relation to the cost of servicing or maintaining neighborhood properties.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-2(b))
832:
(a) The planning and zoning board may impose any additional conditions and development standards, along with the grant of the conditional use, as may be necessary to protect the health, safety and welfare of surrounding landowners, neighborhoods and workers. The planning and zoning board may require as part of its approval, the following conditions:
(1) Planted or screen buffers to reduce adverse or potentially adverse effects on adjoining properties.
(2) Limitation of street accessways, parking areas, and loading docks.
(3) The rearrangement of structures on the development site.
(4) Increases in maximum building height.
(5) Increases in the district requirements for lot size and building line setbacks, but not a reduction of these requirements.
(6) Limitations on the hours of business operation when it can be shown that proposed operational times would cause an adverse effect on adjoining existing uses.
(7) Specified distances from existing residential, public, or institutional developments.
(b) In no case, however, shall the planning and zoning board exempt any conditional use from meeting the minimum lot and structure requirements of the zoning district in which the proposed use is to be located.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-2(c))
835:
(a) The planning and zoning board shall hear and decide applications for variances from the requirements of this chapter, but only in individual cases of practical difficulty or unnecessary hardship. These include:
(1) Exceptional narrowness, shallowness or shape of a specific piece of property, which at the time of adoption of this chapter, was a lot or plat of record; or
(2) Where, by reason of exceptional topographic conditions or other extraordinary or exceptional conditions of a piece of property, the strict application of the development requirements of this chapter would result in practical difficulties to, or undue hardship upon the owner of such property.
(b) However, the planning and zoning board shall not be authorized to grant a density variance or a use variance to permit a use in a district in which the use is prohibited.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-3)
837:
In reviewing an application for a variance, the burden of showing that the variance should be granted shall be upon the person applying therefor.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-3)
838:
The planning and zoning board when granting a variance, may establish reasonable conditions concerning the use of said property and may establish a time period for said variance so that the purpose of this chapter will be served and to provide adequately for the maintenance of the integrity and character of the zone in which such permit is granted.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-3.1)
839:
When necessary, the planning and zoning board may require guarantees, in such form as it deems proper, to insure that conditions designated in connection therewith are being or will be complied with. Where any condition under which a request has been granted appears to have been violated, the planning and zoning board may hold a public hearing thereon to determine whether or not the permit granted shall be terminated.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-3.2)
840:
The planning and zoning board may grant variances from the required improvements and minimum standards of design contained in this chapter, provided the subdivider makes a specific request and shows to the satisfaction of the planning and zoning board that topographical or other conditions peculiar and particular to the site are such that strict adherence to the requirements would cause him unnecessary hardship and would not carry out the intent of these regulations.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-3.3)
841:
The planning and zoning board shall consider and decide whether to grant approval or disapproval of a variance request within 45 days after the public hearing, as specified in this chapter, in accordance with the standards set forth above.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-3.4)
842:
The grant of approval or disapproval of a variance request by the planning and zoning board shall be stated in the minutes with the reasons for departure from the strict application of this article and the conditions under which the variance was granted.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-3.5)
843:
Any variance granted shall terminate automatically when the use ceases to be in full compliance with any conditions imposed by the planning and zoning board, when the use has been abandoned or when the building permit shall have expired.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XII, § 12-3.5)
846:
(a) It shall be unlawful to commence the excavation for or the construction of any building or structure including accessory structures, or to commence the moving, alteration or repair of any structure including accessory structures, until the zoning administrator has issued for such work a building permit containing a statement that the plans, specifications and intended use of such structure in all respects conform with the provisions of this chapter.
(b) No building permit shall be issued for the construction of any building or structure located on a lot or plat subdivided or sold in violation of the provisions of these regulations.
(c) No building permit shall be issued for and no building or other structure shall be erected on any lot within the county unless the street giving access to such lot upon which said building is proposed to be placed shall be accepted and opened as, or shall otherwise receive the legal status of, a public street prior to that time, or unless such street corresponds in its location and lines with a street shown on a plat approved by the planning and zoning board.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-2)
847:
(a) Application for a building permit shall be made in writing to the zoning administrator on forms provided for that purpose. It shall be unlawful for the zoning administrator to approve the plans or issue a building permit for any excavation or construction until he has inspected such plans in detail and found them to be in conformity with this chapter. To this end, the zoning administrator may require that every application for a building permit for excavation, construction, moving or alteration shall be accompanied by a plan or plat drawn to scale and showing the following in sufficient detail to enable the zoning administrator to ascertain whether the proposed excavation, construction, moving or alteration is in conformance with this chapter. The plat shall include:
(1) The actual shape, location and dimensions of the lot to be built upon.
(2) The shape, height, use and location on the lot, building or structures to be erected or altered.
(3) The sizes, locations and use of all existing buildings or structures on the lot.
(4) The number of dwelling units the building, if residential, is designed to accommodate.
(5) The setback lines of building and unloading spaces.
(6) The layout of off-street parking and unloading spaces.
(7) Signature of the county health officer approving the proposed location of the septic tank and field lines where public sewerage is not available.
(8) Such other information concerning the lot or adjoining lots as may be essential in determining whether the provisions of this chapter are being observed.
(b) If the proposed excavation, construction, moving or alteration as set forth in the application for a building permit is in conformity with the provisions of this chapter, the zoning administrator shall issue a building permit for such excavation, construction, moving or alteration.
(c) If the application for a building permit is not approved, the zoning administrator shall state in writing on the application the cause for such disapproval. Issuance of a permit shall, in no case, be construed as waiving any provision of this chapter, and building permits shall be void after six months from date of issue unless substantial progress on the project has been made by that time.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-3)
848:
(a) No land or building or other structure or part thereof hereafter erected, moved or altered in its use shall be occupied or used until the building inspector has issued a certificate of occupancy.
(b) A certificate of occupancy shall be issued in accordance with the provisions of this chapter. If the certificate of occupancy is not granted upon request, the zoning administrator shall state in writing the reasons why the certificate was not granted.
(c) The county shall not issue certificates of occupancy to any owner of a parcel created in violation of these regulations.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIII, § 13-4)
851:
The purpose of this article is to provide for the continuation and within a suitable period of time, elimination of existing uses of property that do not conform to the requirements of this chapter upon its adoption or subsequent amendment.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIV, § 14-1)
852:
(a) The lawful use of any building or structure or land existing at the time of the enactment or subsequent amendment of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived may be continued even though such use does not conform with provisions of this chapter, except that the nonconforming structure or use shall not be:
(1) Changed to another nonconforming use;
(2) Re-established after discontinuance for one year;
(3) Extended or enlarged beyond its size at the time the structure or use become nonconforming. This restriction includes but is not limited to the size of the building, the number of employees, operation during other hours of the day or night, or the use of additional land and additional or more powerful equipment; or
(4) Rebuilt, altered, repaired or replaced after incurring damages exceeding 75 percent or more of its replacement cost at the time or condition except in conformity with this chapter. A nonconforming mobile home may not be replaced after it is removed from the property.
(b) Nothing in this chapter shall be deemed to prevent the strengthening or restoring to safe condition of any building or part thereof declared to be unsafe by any official charged with protecting the public safety, upon order of such official.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIV, § 14-2)
853:
Certain nonconforming signs shall be brought into compliance according to the following schedules:
(1) In all zoning districts, any nonconforming sign cannot be added to or expanded.
(2) In all zoning districts, any nonconforming sign which is damaged to the extent of 75 percent or more of its value must be brought into compliance prior to repair or rehabilitation.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIV, § 14-3)
854:
(a) The zoning administrator shall have the authority to issue a temporary use permit allowing a modular office, manufactured home or travel trailer to be placed on an individual lot for a nonresidential use where the applicant for such permit shows that it is necessary to use such modular office, manufactured home or travel trailer as an office or work area for the preparation and completion of a construction project.
(b) The planning and zoning board may authorize the zoning administrator to issue a temporary hardship permit for medical reasons for a manufactured home or travel trailer in a situation where the unit will be used as an accessory dwelling by a member of the property owner's family. The medical disability must be certified by a physician and the member must be an immediate member of the property owner's family. Also, it must be shown by the applicant that the permit is necessary and the dwelling must be located nearby because the family member requires continuous observation. Once the medical hardship has terminated the temporary accessory dwelling shall be removed.
(c) An application for a temporary use permit authorizing temporary occupancy for the above-mentioned uses shall be submitted to the zoning administrator for approval. The temporary use permit shall be issued by the county for an appropriate period of time not to exceed 12-month increments. The owner of such temporary nonconforming use must agree to remove the temporary use upon expiration of the permit. The applicant can seek permit renewal in one-year increments if necessity continues beyond the initial year.
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XIV, § 14-4)
858:
For the purpose of this chapter, the unincorporated area of the county is divided into the following classes of districts or zones:
(1) Residential zoning districts.
R-A | Residential-Agricultural
R-1 | Low-Density Residential
R-2 | General Residential
R-3 | High-Density Residential
(2) Commercial zoning districts.
C-1 | Neighborhood Commercial
C-2 | General Commercial
C-3 | Heavy Commercial
(3) Industrial zoning districts.
M-1 | Light Industrial
M-2 | General Industrial
(4) Other zoning districts.
P-1 | Professional
PUD | Planned Unit Development
PDD | Planned Development
(Ord. of 7-13-1999(02), art. XV, § 15-1)
859:
(a) The boundaries of the various districts shall be shown on the official zoning map of the county. The official zoning map is hereby made a part of this chapter by reference, and all notations, references and other information shown thereon shall be a part of this chapter as if set forth herein.
(b) The official zoning map, as adopted by the board of commissioners and subsequently amended from time to time by its action, shall be maintained as so revised by the planning and zoning board. The planning and zoning board shall interpret the official zoning map and answer questions concerning district boundary lines and lot lines.

(a) Purpose.
(1) The Jefferson County Board of Commissioners recognizes that farming is a large part of the history and heritage of Jefferson County. The Georgia Supreme Court has determined "a thing that is lawful and proper in one locality may be a nuisance in another. In other words, a nuisance may consist merely of the right thing in the wrong place." May v. Brueshaber, 466 S.E.2d 196,265 Ga. 899 (Ga., 1995). In that same spirit, the board of commissioners requires the proposed dry litter poultry operation will be compatible with the character of the surrounding neighborhood and will not cause hurt, inconvenience, harm or devaluation of adjacent properties. The board of commissioners seeks to find a fair balance between the right to farm and the rights of citizens to be free from unreasonable interference with their right to enjoy and use their property.
(2) In some circumstances, complaints against poultry houses and barns have been associated with allegations of poor management practices by the poultry farmer. This ordinance seeks to establish a complaint resolution process that will provide notice to growers and integrators when complaints are received so that remedial steps can be taken, if necessary, to resolve the complaint.
(3) The Jefferson County Board of Commissioners finds that there is a legitimate public need to adopt this chapter to protect the rights to farms in Jefferson County while also protecting the health, safety, and welfare of its residents from unreasonable interference from certain new large-scale poultry farms.
a. Definition dry litter poultry operation. A dry litter poultry operation (DLPO) in Jefferson County, Georgia is an agricultural enterprise where poultry are kept and raised in concentrated situations. DLPO's congregate poultry, feed, and manure, dead poultry, and production operations on a relatively small land area. Feed is brought to the poultry rather than the poultry grazing or otherwise seeking feed in pastures, fields, or on rangeland. A DLPO is a poultry feeding operation containing or designed to contain more than 125,000 broiler chickens, or 82,000 laying hens or pullets concentration site for more than 30 days during the year.
b. Application submittal requirements. All applications for a permit to operate a dry litter poultry operation shall require a permit issued by the board of commissioners or its designee. The procedure for consideration of the permit shall be the same as a request for re-zoning pursuant to the Jefferson County Code of Ordinances and shall only be allowed in an R-A zone. The following information shall be submitted with a conditional use application.
(4) The design of the chicken houses, stack houses and operations should minimize the impacts of the poultry house on adjacent properties. For example, the ventilation fan exhausts should be directed away from the closest property lines of adjoining properties.
(b) Additional requirements, review criteria, and standards.
(1) Odors, noise and dust. Dry litter poultry operations shall be operated in such a manner as to not constitute a nuisance as defined by law or cause hurt, inconvenience, harm or devaluation of adjacent properties due to emissions of odors, dust or particulate matter.
(2) Character of the neighborhood and surrounding community. The board of commissioners should consider the concentration of dry litter poultry operations in the area; zoning classification of adjacent properties; level of traffic, driveway locations and road conditions; DLPO's may be 24-hour per day operations; scale and design of buildings; noise, odor or vibration; proximity of existing residences; and, similar impacts associated with the proposed land use.
(3) Nuisance. No dry litter poultry operation shall be operated as a nuisance. See O.C.G.A. §41-1-1.
(4) Setbacks. The specific setback requirements for dry litter poultry operations set forth herein are intended to minimize the adverse effects commonly associated with such operations, provided that larger setbacks or other conditions may be imposed as conditions so as to minimize adverse effects on surrounding property in cases involving, but not limited to, uncommonly large operations, unusual topographic conditions, or proximity to sensitive natural, scenic, or historic areas, municipal boundaries, and residential areas.
a. No dry litter poultry operation shall be constructed in any location where any portion of the confinement area is 200 feet or less from the property boundaries of the parcel on which the confinement area is to be constructed.
b. No dry litter poultry operation shall be constructed in any locations where any portion of the confinement area is 500 feet or less from any residence.
c. No dry litter poultry operation shall be constructed in any location where any portion of the confinement area is 1,500 feet or less from any building or property that is regularly used as a school, hospital, church, a public park, a public recreational area, a senior center, a nursing home or retirement home, a restaurant, or public community center.
d. No dry litter poultry operation shall be constructed in any location where any portion of the confinement area is 200 feet or less from any perennial stream.
(5) Air quality protection. The County and Ordinance Officer may refer to and use State and Federal air quality standards and guidelines in determinations of appropriateness and enforcement.
(6) Dead poultry disposal. Dead poultry shall be disposed of in a way that does not adversely affect ground or surface water and does not compromise public health. Any dead poultry shall be disposed of upon discovery by removal for rendering, incineration, burial or composting as approved by the Georgia Department of Agriculture and by the Environmental Protection Division of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources.
(c) Complaint process. The county ordinance officer shall be authorized to investigate allegations of violations of this code section as he would other code and ordinance violations in Jefferson County. In addition, if the ordinance officer receives a credible complaint that a dry litter poultry operation has become a nuisance or is in violation of the codes and ordinances of Jefferson County, he should follow the following complaint resolution process.
(1) The complaint should be documented in writing including the date, name and address of the complainant and nature of the complaint. The ordinance officer should contact the grower or its agent and inform him/her of the nature of the complaint. The grower will assist the ordinance officer in the investigation of the complaint including compliance with bio-security protocols and access to the property subject to the complaint for inspection.
(2) As soon as practical, the ordinance officer will visit the dry litter poultry operation and investigate the complaint. If violations are found or probable cause exists to believe the operation is not in conformance with Jefferson County Codes or Ordinances, the ordinance officer will inform the owner, operator or his agent on the premises of the violation. The ordinance officer will determine if a citation should be issued based upon the nature or severity of the violation. If the ordinance officer believes that probable cause exists that the operation constitutes a nuisance or is in violation of the law, he may also notify the appropriate departments in State and Federal Government and regulatory agencies that may have jurisdiction such as the EPA, EPD, and the Department of Agriculture;
a. While remediation or elimination is preferred, it will not serve as a defense to a violation, but may be considered in mitigation of punishment.
